headlines.title: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh declines to signal a near-term rate move at IMF fireside chat; reiterates price stability priority
headlines.summary: At the IMF/World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on 2026-10-16, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said he would not prejudge upcoming FOMC moves and emphasized price stability; reporting indicates his remarks did not provide a clear October meeting signal.

evidence.description: AP report summarizing Warsh remarks at the IMF meeting on Oct 16, 2026.
evidence.exact_excerpt: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said Friday he won't prejudge what the U.S. central bank will do about interest rates at its upcoming meetings in October and December.

evidence.description: Published transcript/coverage of the Warsh-Georgieva discussion (event page/transcript feed).
evidence.exact_excerpt: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva joins US Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh in Bangkok ... for a conversation on the key forces reshaping the global economy.

headlines.claim_evidence_note: Cited authority cited_authority_unavailable_or_not_inspected; literal excerpt presence is not semantic proof.
headlines.attribution: AP reporting (Oct 16, 2026) and event transcript/coverage of the IMF fireside chat.
headlines.what_is_known: Warsh spoke publicly at IMF/World Bank meetings on Oct 16, 2026 and said he would not pre-commit to specific policy moves; he emphasized price stability.
headlines.uncertainty: No contemporaneous FOMC decision or Fed press release on Oct 16; future policy path remains decided at FOMC meetings. Statements are subject to later Fed clarification.
headlines.what_cannot_be_concluded: You cannot conclude from these remarks alone that the Fed will hold or change rates at the October 27–28 FOMC meeting.
headlines.resolution_needed: Official FOMC statement, minutes, or Fed press release (next FOMC meeting) to determine formal policy changes.

headlines.title: AI/data-center bellwether CoreWeave's bonds trade at distressed levels; market scrutiny of AI buildout financing intensifies
headlines.summary: Historical context (event 2026-10-14): Multiple financial outlets reported Oct 14–16, 2026 that CoreWeave's corporate bonds plunged and yields rose sharply, prompting commentary that the sell-off is a market test of financing for large AI-focused data centers; coverage indicates notable bond-market stress (e.g., high yields, CDS pricing) but no insolvency filing in the cited period.

evidence.description: Reuters analysis of CoreWeave's bond sell-off and market implications (Oct 16, 2026).
evidence.exact_excerpt: Loss-making and deeply indebted US cloud company CoreWeave became an easy target this week for investors concerned about an artificial intelligence bubble.

evidence.description: Axios coverage noting CoreWeave bond sell-off and market commentary (Oct 16, 2026).
evidence.exact_excerpt: Investors have been selling off CoreWeave's bonds for weeks, worried that the revenues from AI may not be enough to sustain its growing debt burden.

headlines.claim_evidence_note: Cited authority cited_authority_unavailable_or_not_inspected; literal excerpt presence is not semantic proof.
headlines.attribution: Reuters (Oct 16, 2026); Axios (Oct 16, 2026); Bloomberg coverage referenced by other outlets.
headlines.what_is_known: Bond yields on CoreWeave paper surged and market commentary labeled the bonds distressed; this has market-significance implications for AI data-center financing.
headlines.uncertainty: Public reporting shows market prices and analyst commentary but does not prove default or creditor action as of Oct 16, 2026.
headlines.what_cannot_be_concluded: Cannot conclude CoreWeave has filed for bankruptcy or that counterparties have ceased business without explicit court filings or company notices.
headlines.resolution_needed: Primary corporate filings (SEC Form 8-K), trustee/creditor notices, or a company press release confirming default or restructuring if one occurs.

headlines.title: Mortgage rates remain elevated in the latest weekly survey; 30-year fixed near recent highs
headlines.summary: Historical context (event 2026-10-08): Freddie Mac's most recent weekly PMMS (covering week to Oct 8, 2026) shows the 30-year fixed mortgage averaging about 7.40%; independent US reporting (AP) reiterated mortgage rates are near the highest in roughly three years as of mid-October.

evidence.description: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS) weekly average for 30-year fixed as published in October 2026.
evidence.exact_excerpt: The 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 7.40% as of October 8, 2026, up from last week when it averaged 7.28%.

evidence.description: AP summary reporting the same Freddie Mac rate and context (mortgage rates near 3-year highs).
evidence.exact_excerpt: The benchmark 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was unchanged from last week at 7.40%, mortgage buyer Freddie Mac said Thursday.

headlines.claim_evidence_note: Cited authority cited_source_does_not_confirm_position; literal excerpt presence is not semantic proof.
headlines.what_is_known: The published Freddie Mac PMMS shows a 30-year fixed average of 7.40% as of Oct 8, 2026; news outlets report this as the most recent weekly figure.
headlines.uncertainty: Freddie Mac's weekly PMMS updates weekly; intraday broker quotes and secondary-market movements can differ. More recent daily broker snapshots may vary from PMMS.
headlines.what_cannot_be_concluded: This PMMS figure alone does not determine individual lender offers or daily mortgage-rate fluctuations after Oct 8, 2026.
headlines.resolution_needed: Later-week PMMS release (next scheduled weekly release) or intraday MBS-market data for rates after Oct 8, 2026, if needed.
headlines.temporal_caveat: Historical event, not established as new
